newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insurers say car accident payouts to rise.
newsitem.headline: German insurers say car accident payouts to rise.

text.p: The minimum amount paid by German insurers for clients who injure someone in a car accident will be raised significantly as of July 1, the industry association of German car insurers (GDV) said on Thursday.

The GDV said in a statement that the justice ministry plans to raise the minimum payout to five million marks for one injured party and 15 million marks for three or more injured parties. The current minimum requirements are one million marks for one injured person and 1.5 million when several people are injured.
The GDV expected most insurers to raise premiums from January 1, 1998 to cover the costs of the new requirements.
Separately, the GDV said Germans are becoming increasingly less scrupulous about making bogus insurance claims.
In a survey conducted by the association, between 25 and 40 percent of people asked said they had in the past filed a bogus insurance claim.
GDV's Chairman Bruno Gas said the estimated cost to insurance companies from such claims was around five billion marks in 1996.
